{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|&hellip;with the galaxy plunged into darkness by war and disease, Mandalore the Uniter called the best and brightest Mandalorians home from the distant stars to which fate had cast them. The Return strengthened Mandalore, which emerged as a rival of the Republic.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
The '''Return''' was a movement started by the veteran [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Mandalore the Uniter|Aga Awaud]]. Amidst the tumultuous era of the [[New Sith Wars]], Awaud had journeyed home to [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]—the Mandalorians' cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]—only to discover that [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian space]] was under attack by [[Pirate/Legends|raiders]] from the surrounding [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], and most of [[Clan Awaud/Legends|his clan]] had perished from an outbreak of the [[Candorian plague/Legends|Candorian plague]] that was ravaging [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Faced with the loss of his family and a Mandalore sector so insecure that Mandalorian [[Starship/Legends|starships]] were forced to form defensive caravans just to survive, Awaud was spurred to action: in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[1058 BBY]], he called upon Mandalorians living throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] to rally to the defense of Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Many heeded Awaud's summons, and the mass migration of Mandalorians that made their way back to Mandalore became known as the Return. Aga Awaud went on to claim the title of [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] and the sobriquet "Mandalore the Uniter;"<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> with a renewed population, Mandalore grew stronger under his reign,<ref name="TBHC" /> not only surviving the chaos of the New [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Wars, but flourishing. As a result of the Return, Mandalore became a regional industrial power and a symbol of much-needed stability in the galaxy's [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], offering protection to neighboring [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and sectors.<ref name="TEGW" />

Nearly a thousand years later, [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] [[Tor Vizsla]] considered the Return to be a pivotal moment in Mandalorian history, detailing the movement, its founder, and their importance in a manifesto entitled ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]''.<ref name="TBHC" /> In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], close to a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] after the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|devastated]] Mandalore during the course of their invasion of the known galaxy, reigning ''Mand'alor'' [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] enacted a decree similar to the Return of old. Fett recalled two million Mandalorians from across the galaxy to bolster the planet's population and rebuild from the damage inflicted by the Yuuzhan Vong, leading to an eventual economic resurgence on Mandalore.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Return movement was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', a multi-subject reference guide co-[[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]], published [[April 3]], [[2012]].<ref name="TEGW" /> The following year, ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'' was released, further referencing the Return and its impact on Mandalorian history.<ref name="TBHC" />
